subject: Renewal structure proposal — staged GPU ramp & co-term
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nimbus.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal structure proposal — staged GPU ramp & co-term

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier this week. Per our discussion I put together a proposed structure that should address Nimbus's capacity growth and procurement preference to co-term with your analytics platform deal. High level:

- Term: 36 months (Mar 1, 2027 — Feb 28, 2030) with an option to convert to month-to-month in year three at a reduced committed capacity.
- Ramp: staged committed GPU capacity that increases each 12-month anniversary (details attached).
- Pricing: blended committed rate with step-down discounts as commitment grows (see attached spreadsheet).
- Auto-renew: 12-month auto-renew by default unless written notice 60 days prior; we can make auto-renew opt-out via procurement request.
- Co-terming: we can align Redwood contract to your analytics platform co-term date; this requires a short amendment to map Redwood committed capacity to the partner billing milestone.

I've attached a draft amendment and a proposed ramp schedule for your review (Redwood_Renewal_Amendment_v1.pdf; Capacity_Ramp_Schedule_XLSX.xlsx). Key asks from you: confirm preferred co-term date (if different from Mar 1), preferred ramp percentages, and whether procurement needs any additional billing language for co-term.

If it helps, we can put the ramp as an explicit schedule in the SOW so your procurement team has clear milestones for capacity increase and billing.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm co-term date and procurement constraints by EOD Thursday 2/11.
2) We incorporate any redlines and send to DocuSign the week of 2/14.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this locked.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Sean —

Appreciate the clear proposal and attachments. A few quick items from procurement/finance:

- Procurement would prefer a co-term date of 06/30/2027 (we have an existing analytics contract that renews then). Is there flexibility to set the effective co-term to 6/30 while starting committed capacity on 3/1?
- Can you send a line-item view (annual billing rows) so finance can run an ARR forecast?
- For auto-renew: we need to confirm the notice window. 60 days is likely OK but will check with legal for mandatory language.

Also copying Ethan (legal lead) — Ethan, can you flag anything specific we need in the amendment for co-term mapping?

Thanks — I can review the amendment in detail by Friday 2/12.

Thanks Olivia — that's helpful. Short answers and clarifications:

- Co-term flexibility: yes, we can set the contract co-term to 06/30/2027 and make the first ramp milestone effective 03/01/2027. The amendment will include a clause mapping Redwood billing periods to your partner milestone.

- Line-item view: attached a 3-line annual billing breakdown (see Capacity_Ramp_Schedule_XLSX.xlsx). Summary below:
  * Year 1 (3/1/27—2/28/28): committed 40 GPUs (billed monthly or annually) — blended committed rate $X/ GPU-hour (see sheet)
  * Year 2 (3/1/28—2/28/29): committed 70 GPUs
  * Year 3 (3/1/29—2/28/30): committed 120 GPUs; option to transition to monthly billing for excess usage beyond committed baseline
\- Discounts: 8% step discount when moving from Year 1 -> Year 2; additional 6% on Year 3 if signed for the 36-month term.
\- Auto-renew notice: we can change to 90 days if procurement prefers — happy to make that editable in the amendment.

Folks from Sales Ops/Rev (cc'd) — any constraints on the discount stacking or minimums?

If Olivia is comfortable with co-term 6/30 and the ramp numbers above, I'll get the amendment updated and route to DocuSign next Monday.

Best,
Sean

1) Discount stacking (8% then 6%) OK from pricing ops?
2) Any compliance/SLA language we should proactively add for a ramp schedule (customer asked for mapping to partner milestone)?

Sean —

Quick runbook: pricing ops reviewed — discount stacking OK provided the contract lists the effective committed GPU counts per year and there is a floor for minimum monthly billing (we use 75% of committed as the minimum billed baseline). Suggest we update ramp to: 40 GPUs (Y1), 65 GPUs (Y2), 110 GPUs (Y3) to better align with historical utilization from Nimbus (they've under-utilized past peaks).

Legal note: for co-term mapping we'll add a clause that ties Redwood invoicing to the co-term milestone but explicitly disclaims partner liability for Nimbus's partner charges. Also recommend an SLA credit if Redwood fails to meet >48hr sustained capacity availability during a ramp window (simple credit formula: 1% of monthly committed spend per incident, up to 6%).

Lauren — please confirm billing language and DocuSign template to use. Sean — once Lauren confirms I'll approve and you can send updated amendment to Olivia.

-Marissa
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Olivia —

Thanks for the quick review and to Marissa/LAuren for ops/legal input. To summarize the agreed updates before I route to DocuSign:

- Co-term: contract co-term set to 06/30/2027 while committed capacity starts 03/01/2027.
- Ramp schedule (finalized): Year 1: 40 GPUs; Year 2: 65 GPUs; Year 3: 110 GPUs.
- Pricing: step discounts (8% Year2, +6% Year3) as discussed. Minimum billed baseline = 75% of committed.
- Auto-renew: 90-day notice for non-renewal (editable by procurement).
- SLA: credit for sustained capacity outages during ramp windows (per Marissa's suggested formula).

I will upload the amended doc to DocuSign Monday (link will be sent). Expect one final legal clause around partner liability mapping — Ethan, if you can send any redlines before Monday EOD we'll try to incorporate them into the initial send.

Next steps:
1) Sean to route DocuSign on Mon 2/15 (target).
2) Olivia/procurement to sign within 7 business days for the March 1 effective start.

If that timeline works, I'll send the DocuSign link tomorrow.

Thanks —
